# VirtuMic **The General Purpose Virtual Microphone for Android™.**
## Introduction VirtuMic is a framework and an app for creating virtual microphones on Android. It's based on the system's built-in audio routing framework to inject audio back into the system as a live microphone feed. ## Download App ### [Releases](https://gitlab.com/IndiDevs/VirtuMic/-/releases) #### [Mirror](https://github.com/IndiTheo/VirtuMic/releases) ## Requirements - **Android Version**: Android 13 (API 33) or higher. - **Permissions**: `MODIFY_AUDIO_ROUTING` and `CAPTURE_AUDIO_OUTPUT`. Can be acquired via one of the options below. - **ADB Shell Context (rootless)**: Wireless ADB debugging. - **Rooted Device**: Systemless overlay (Magisk) module for automated privilege escalation. ## Features ### Audio - 🎵📁 Stream audio files — ✅ - 📱 Capture and stream apps' audio — ✅ - 📞 Call module — ❌ ⏰ (Planned) ### Operation Modes - Media3 MediaSessionService (for the app) — ✅ - MediaSessionService for 3rd-party apps — ❌ ⏰ (Planned) - Media3 Cast — ❌ 🗣️ (TBD) ### Privilege Modes - ADB (Android 13+) — ✅ - Magic Mount Overlay — ✅ - Shizuku — ❌ ⏰ (Planned) ## How it Works VirtuMic creates a virtual microphone by redirecting audio within the Android system: - **System Audio Management**: Android routes audio from sources to sinks (speakers). VirtuMic uses a loopback `AudioPolicy` to intercept this flow. - **Loopback Policy**: VirtuMic registers a policy that captures any audio intended for recording. Instead of getting sound from the physical microphone, the system is told to pull it from a specific internal injection track that is defined by the policy. - **Injection**: When you enable streaming, VirtuMic writes the audio data directly into this injection track. Because of the policy, the system treats this data as a live microphone feed, making it available to any app on your device. For a technical explanation, refer to the module READMEs: [Core Engine](virtumic-core/README.md), [Audio Service](virtumic-service/README.md). ## Developers VirtuMic is structured as a multi-module library framework. In addition to the client app, the project provides core modules for library integration: ### [VirtuMic Core (`virtumic-core`)](virtumic-core/README.md) The high-performance virtual microphone engine for Android. It enables Android applications to create virtual audio policies, bridging the native gap in inter-app audio sharing. The library intercepts PCM streams from apps or manual sources and injects them into the system microphone. It provides `VMicEngine`, a privilege-agnostic entry point to deploy virtual microphone sinks. For further details, see the [Core README](virtumic-core/README.md). ### [VirtuMic Service (`virtumic-service`)](virtumic-service/README.md) A privileged Media3 `MediaSessionService` for virtual microphone audio injection. It exposes a `MediaSessionService` interface, allowing external controllers and UI clients to control virtual microphone streaming, app capture loopbacks, and file playback pipelines over standard Media3 `MediaController` APIs. Host applications supply a `VMicEngine` instance via `VMicEngineProvider`, and clients connect using Media3 `MediaController` with custom parameters. For further details, see the [Service README](virtumic-service/README.md). ## Audio Quirks - **16-bit PCM Enforcement**: All capture and injection streams are strictly locked to 16-bit PCM integer (`ENCODING_PCM_16BIT`), required by Android's `REMOTE_SUBMIX` and HAL audio policies. - **Stereo vs Mono Recording Apps**: When streaming in stereo mode, Android's `AudioFlinger` automatically downmixes stereo virtual microphone input to mono if the recording app requests mono (`AudioFormat.CHANNEL_IN_MONO`). To verify or record true stereo separation, use a recording app that explicitly supports stereo microphone capture (`CHANNEL_IN_STEREO`). ## Release Verification ### APK Signing Certificate Ensure the app comes from the official developer: - **SHA-256 Fingerprint**: `E9:8E:67:C5:20:FA:02:E3:E4:83:8C:1C:0C:EE:33:50:BB:0C:84:3B:B0:6B:35:88:D5:6E:7F:60:45:C6:E2:7B` - Verify locally: ```bash apksigner verify --print-certs virtumic-full.apk ``` *(Compare the output SHA-256 certificate digest printed by `apksigner` against the pinned fingerprint above).* ### Keyless Cosign Verification (Sigstore OIDC) Verify that `checksums.txt` was created by CI on the official repository (`main` branch): ```bash cosign verify-blob \ --bundle checksums.txt.bundle \ --certificate-oidc-issuer "https://gitlab.com" \ --certificate-identity "https://gitlab.com/IndiDevs/VirtuMic//.gitlab-ci.yml@refs/heads/main" \ checksums.txt ``` ### Asset Integrity (Optional) Ensure the released assets come from the official developer and haven't been corrupted or altered: - **Pinned GPG Key Fingerprint**: `20BE44F0EA96B41F6FA2B07D29AA514BF4637181` - Make sure your downloaded APK and `checksums.txt` are placed together in the same folder before running: ```bash # 1. Fetch and verify GPG signature of checksums.txt gpg --keyserver hkps://keyserver.ubuntu.com --recv-keys 20BE44F0EA96B41F6FA2B07D29AA514BF4637181 gpg --fingerprint 20BE44F0EA96B41F6FA2B07D29AA514BF4637181 gpg --verify checksums.txt.asc checksums.txt # 2. Verify downloaded APK matches the hash in checksums.txt sha256sum -c checksums.txt --ignore-missing ``` *(If successful, `sha256sum` prints `virtumic-full.apk: OK` or similar, confirming the asset matches the verified checksums).* ## Contributing & Support You can help improve the project or get help: - If you encounter issues or want to request a feature, open an issue - If you want to contribute code, feel free to open a PR See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for directions. ## Acknowledgements - [flyfishxu / Kadb](https://github.com/flyfishxu/Kadb) - prominent [POC](https://github.com/Genymobile/scrcpy/issues/3880#issuecomment-1595722119) in the field by [yume-chan](https://github.com/yume-chan) - [Taming Bazel Dependency Conflicts: An Android Case Study / Taufik Amaryansyah](https://medium.com/@taufik.amary/taming-bazel-dependency-conflicts-an-android-case-study-44b7926839be) - [Building a Modern Android Music Player App with Bazel, Jetpack Compose, and ExoPlayer / Taufik Amaryansyah](https://medium.com/@taufik.amary/building-a-modern-android-music-player-app-with-bazel-jetpack-compose-and-exoplayer-4a70039655f2) ## Notice - This project is an independent development and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with Google LLC or any of its subsidiaries. VirtuMic

The General Purpose Virtual Microphone for Android™.

Introduction

VirtuMic is a framework and an app for creating virtual microphones on Android. It's based

on the system's built-in audio routing framework to inject audio back into the system

as a live microphone feed.

Download App

[Releases](https://gitlab.com/IndiDevs/VirtuMic/-/releases)

#### Mirror

Requirements

  • **Android Version**: Android 13 (API 33) or higher.
  • **Permissions**: `MODIFY_AUDIO_ROUTING` and `CAPTURE_AUDIO_OUTPUT`.

    • Can be acquired via one of the options below.

    - ADB Shell Context (rootless): Wireless ADB debugging.

    - Rooted Device: Systemless overlay (Magisk) module for automated privilege escalation.

    Features

    Audio

  • 🎵📁 Stream audio files — ✅
  • 📱 Capture and stream apps' audio — ✅
  • 📞 Call module — ❌ ⏰ (Planned)

    • Operation Modes

  • Media3 MediaSessionService (for the app) — ✅
  • MediaSessionService for 3rd-party apps — ❌ ⏰ (Planned)
  • Media3 Cast — ❌ 🗣️ (TBD)

    • Privilege Modes

  • ADB (Android 13+) — ✅
  • Magic Mount Overlay — ✅
  • Shizuku — ❌ ⏰ (Planned)

    • How it Works

    VirtuMic creates a virtual microphone by redirecting audio within the Android system:

  • **System Audio Management**: Android routes audio from sources to sinks (speakers).

    • VirtuMic uses a loopback AudioPolicy to intercept this flow.

  • **Loopback Policy**: VirtuMic registers a policy that captures any audio intended for recording.

    • Instead of getting sound from the physical microphone, the system is told to pull it from a

    specific internal injection track that is defined by the policy.

  • **Injection**: When you enable streaming, VirtuMic writes the audio data directly into this

    • injection track. Because of the policy, the system treats this data as a live microphone feed,

    making it available to any app on your device.

    For a technical explanation, refer to the module READMEs: Core Engine, Audio Service.

    Developers

    VirtuMic is structured as a multi-module library framework. In addition to the client app, the project provides core modules for library integration:

    [VirtuMic Core (`virtumic-core`)](virtumic-core/README.md)

    The high-performance virtual microphone engine for Android. It enables Android

    applications to create virtual audio policies, bridging the native gap in

    inter-app audio sharing. The library intercepts PCM streams from apps or manual sources

    and injects them into the system microphone. It provides VMicEngine, a privilege-agnostic

    entry point to deploy virtual microphone sinks. For further details, see the Core README.

    [VirtuMic Service (`virtumic-service`)](virtumic-service/README.md)

    A privileged Media3 MediaSessionService for virtual microphone audio injection.

    It exposes a MediaSessionService interface, allowing external controllers

    and UI clients to control virtual microphone streaming, app capture loopbacks,

    and file playback pipelines over standard Media3 MediaController APIs.

    Host applications supply a VMicEngine instance via VMicEngineProvider,

    and clients connect using Media3 MediaController with custom parameters. For further details, see the Service README.

    Audio Quirks

  • **16-bit PCM Enforcement**: All capture and injection streams are strictly locked to 16-bit PCM integer (`ENCODING_PCM_16BIT`), required by Android's `REMOTE_SUBMIX` and HAL audio policies.
  • **Stereo vs Mono Recording Apps**: When streaming in stereo mode, Android's `AudioFlinger` automatically downmixes stereo virtual microphone input to mono if the recording app requests mono (`AudioFormat.CHANNEL_IN_MONO`). To verify or record true stereo separation, use a recording app that explicitly supports stereo microphone capture (`CHANNEL_IN_STEREO`).

    • Release Verification

    APK Signing Certificate

    Ensure the app comes from the official developer:

  • **SHA-256 Fingerprint**: `E9:8E:67:C5:20:FA:02:E3:E4:83:8C:1C:0C:EE:33:50:BB:0C:84:3B:B0:6B:35:88:D5:6E:7F:60:45:C6:E2:7B`
  • Verify locally:

    • ```bash

    apksigner verify --print-certs virtumic-full.apk

    ```

    *(Compare the output SHA-256 certificate digest printed by apksigner against the pinned fingerprint above).*

    Keyless Cosign Verification (Sigstore OIDC)

    Verify that checksums.txt was created by CI on the official repository (main branch):

    cosign verify-blob \
  --bundle checksums.txt.bundle \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer "https://gitlab.com" \
  --certificate-identity "https://gitlab.com/IndiDevs/VirtuMic//.gitlab-ci.yml@refs/heads/main" \
  checksums.txt

    Asset Integrity (Optional)

    Ensure the released assets come from the official developer and haven't been corrupted or altered:

  • **Pinned GPG Key Fingerprint**: `20BE44F0EA96B41F6FA2B07D29AA514BF4637181`
  • Make sure your downloaded APK and `checksums.txt` are placed together in the same folder before running:

    • ```bash

    # 1. Fetch and verify GPG signature of checksums.txt

    gpg --keyserver hkps://keyserver.ubuntu.com --recv-keys 20BE44F0EA96B41F6FA2B07D29AA514BF4637181

    gpg --fingerprint 20BE44F0EA96B41F6FA2B07D29AA514BF4637181

    gpg --verify checksums.txt.asc checksums.txt

    # 2. Verify downloaded APK matches the hash in checksums.txt

    sha256sum -c checksums.txt --ignore-missing

    ```

    *(If successful, sha256sum prints virtumic-full.apk: OK or similar, confirming the asset matches the verified checksums).*

    Contributing & Support

    You can help improve the project or get help:

  • If you encounter issues or want to request a feature, open an issue
  • If you want to contribute code, feel free to open a PR

    • See CONTRIBUTING.md for directions.

    Acknowledgements

  • [flyfishxu / Kadb](https://github.com/flyfishxu/Kadb)
  • prominent [POC](https://github.com/Genymobile/scrcpy/issues/3880#issuecomment-1595722119) in the

    • field by yume-chan

  • [Taming Bazel Dependency Conflicts: An Android Case Study / Taufik Amaryansyah](https://medium.com/@taufik.amary/taming-bazel-dependency-conflicts-an-android-case-study-44b7926839be)
  • [Building a Modern Android Music Player App with Bazel, Jetpack Compose, and ExoPlayer / Taufik Amaryansyah](https://medium.com/@taufik.amary/building-a-modern-android-music-player-app-with-bazel-jetpack-compose-and-exoplayer-4a70039655f2)
